issues.description: Method: SealSaloon.orderMeal(Meal). The problem statement UML and textual specification declare orderMeal(Meal) with return type void (UML: +orderMeal(Meal): void and multiple textual references describe it as a void operation). The solution implementation declares public boolean orderMeal(Meal meal) (solution file SealSaloon.java). This mismatch between void (spec) and boolean (solution) creates ambiguity for students about the expected signature and return value semantics and may lead to incompatible implementations or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the orderMeal signature consistent across artifacts. Preferred resolution: change the solution implementation to match the specification by declaring public void orderMeal(Meal meal) (remove boolean return values and returns). Alternatively, if the boolean return value conveys useful information, update the problem statement UML and textual description to declare orderMeal(Meal): boolean and document the meaning of the returned value. Ensure tests and examples are updated accordingly.

issues.description: Attribute: SealSaloon.stock. The problem statement first instructs that a final Stock stock should be initialized in the SealSaloon constructor (instance initialization), but elsewhere in the same problem text it explicitly states the stock attribute must be static (shared across instances) and that acceptSupplyDelivery/calculateTotalPrice should be static and use the shared stock. This is a contradiction: initializing a shared (static) attribute in an instance constructor conflicts with the requirement that the stock be static/final.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification so it is not self-contradictory. Option A (recommended to match solution/tests): state explicitly that stock is a static final field shared by all SealSaloon instances and should be initialized at its declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Specify that orders is an instance (non-static) Meal[] and should be initialized in the instance constructor. Option B (if the intent was instance-level stock): remove the requirement that stock be static and update the statements about static methods accordingly. Update the problem text and UML so only one consistent approach is specified.
